sections.h2: What is Pembroke Pines, and who buys homes here?
sections.html:
Pembroke Pines is a large city in southwest Broward County, and the city says it has over 170,000 residents. It sits near major highways and interstates, employment centers, parks and golf courses.

It was incorporated on January 16, 1960, when it was the Village of Pembroke Pines with about 1,500 residents. After Hurricane Andrew in 1992 the city's own history says it became the fastest growing city in the country, which is why so much housing dates from the 1990s and later.

Buyers here range from families drawn to its schools and parks to residents of the Century Village area. The city counts 41 arts and cultural facilities and describes its mission around raising a family.

sections.h2: How did Pembroke Pines grow, and what does that mean for house age?
sections.html:
The area was open land and small communities, including the Pembroke Pines Country Club development, in the mid 20th century. Fire stations opened as the city expanded: Station 79 in 1981 in land annexed west of US 27 and Station 89 in 1986 at Century Village.

  • Land west of US 27 was annexed by 1981, so house age varies by side of town.
  • Check roof, electrical and plumbing age on your own house.
  • Ask a title agent what recorded items exist on your lot.

Knowing your home's age helps you decide whether a cash offer or listing fits. The city now serves residents from six fire stations and, in 2014, joined the Broward County Regional 911 system.

sections.h2: What does Florida charge to transfer a Pembroke Pines house?
sections.html:
Doc stamps on a deed are 70 cents per $100 of consideration in Broward County, as the revenue department lists every county except Miami-Dade. All parties to the document are liable.

Taxable documents the state lists for real estate transfers
DocumentTaxed by DOR?
Warranty deedYes
Quit claim deedYes
Deed in lieu of foreclosureYes
Personal representative deed under probated willNot taxable

The clerk of court collects the tax when recording. Ask your closing agent to apply the rate to your price in writing.

sections.h2: How does the Broward County tax cycle affect a seller?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser values your home as of January 1 and takes exemption applications through March 1. The office's site lists 954-357-6830 and weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

  • TRIM notices mail in August.
  • Bills go out in November with a 4 percent discount for paying that month.
  • Taxes go delinquent April 1.

Your closing agent prorates the year between you and the buyer. Make sure the prorated amount uses the right exemption status.

sections.h2: Does homestead or portability matter if I leave Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
Yes, especially for owners who have held a home for years. Save Our Homes holds yearly assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or CPI, and portability lets you carry up to $500,000 of that benefit to a new Florida home.

You must establish the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned. File Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1. The statute page notes later amendments first apply to the 2027 roll, so confirm current rules.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Florida sets clocks for each. Summary administration is available for non-exempt estates up to $150,000, creditors have the later of three months after publication or 30 days after service to file, and foreclosure sales run 20 to 35 days after judgment.

For tenants, a nonpayment notice is 3 days, and a 7 day cure applies to many lease breaches. These details can change an offer, so gather the documents first.

sections.h2: How does Pembroke Pines handle public safety and services that buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city's fire rescue department runs six stations, and Pembroke Pines became the South Region answering point in the Broward County Regional 911 system in 2014. The department earned a Class 1 ISO rating in 1998, which the city's history says only 57 of 44,000 departments held then.

Insurance rating and response data are useful to mention to buyers, and your agent can confirm the current rating for your address.

sections.h2: What about tax certificates and tax deeds in Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. After two years a holder can apply for a tax deed with a $75 application fee, and the clerk runs the auction.

The opening bid on a homestead includes one half of the latest assessed value. If you are behind, ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff and weigh a sale before a deed application.

  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Senior deferral uses Form DR-570 by March 31.

sections.h2: Can seniors and veterans cut a Pembroke Pines tax bill?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older may get an additional exemption of up to $50,000 if the local ordinance allows and income is within limit. Disabled veterans may receive a $5,000 assessed value reduction, and veterans 65 or older with a service-connected disability may get a discount equal to the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may receive an exemption proportional to the time deployed, and may rent out a homestead without abandoning it. Ask the property appraiser about proof needed.

sections.h2: What are the risks of an informal family transfer in Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
The state treats any transfer of legal or beneficial title as a change of ownership, with listed exceptions for spouses and certain transfers at death. Quit claim deeds are taxable documents.

A written conveyance of land must be signed before two witnesses under the state statute. Use a title agent to prepare it correctly.

sections.h2: What steps should I take to prepare a Pembroke Pines sale?
sections.html:
Start with paperwork. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill, any association documents, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions.

Then compare a listing, a for sale by owner path and a cash offer by what you net, not by headline price. Ask for the offer in writing and read it in full.

faqs.a: January 16, 1960, according to the city. It was then the Village of Pembroke Pines with about 1,500 residents.

faqs.q: What doc stamp rate applies in Pembroke Pines?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration, since Broward is not Miami-Dade. The rate is listed on the state revenue page.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings?
faqs.a: Possibly. Portability can carry up to $500,000 of the difference to a new Florida homestead within three years.
All parties to the document are liable under the state's rule, so the contract should say who pays.

faqs.q: Is inherited property taxed on transfer?
faqs.a: A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable, but other transfers can be, so confirm with a title agent.
